note.content:
Repro (headless, no GUI needed):
  cargo run --release -p kopitiam-pdf --example annots -- ~/Desktop/test-annotation.pdf
  => /Ink x25, with /AP: 0/25, painted inside /Rect: 0/25  <-- INVISIBLE  (exit 1)

Cross-checked against two other engines on the same file, page 1, 150dpi:
  * poppler (pdftoppm, Okular's backend): 10821 blue annotation pixels -- visible
  * hayro 0.7.1 rendered directly       : 0/25 painted -- blank too
  * kopitiam native                     : 0/25 painted -- blank

DIAGNOSIS -- two independent gaps, neither is a mistranslation of the existing
port. The port is a correct SUBSET; these files were simply never ported.

1. CONSUME gap: nothing on the render path ever reads /Annots. run_page()
   gathers only /Contents (page_run.rs gather_contents). A page's /Annots is a
   sibling of /Contents. MuPDF's fz_run_page = pdf_run_page_contents +
   pdf_run_page_annots; only the first half exists here.
   Upstream: pdf-run.c:353 pdf_run_page_annots -> :27 pdf_run_annot_with_usage;
   pdf-annot.c:194 pdf_annot_transform (PDF 32000-1 s12.5.5 BBox->Rect).

2. PRODUCE gap: this file has NO /AP anywhere (0/25). Okular writes ink annots
   as data only (/InkList, /C, /Border) and expects the viewer to synthesise
   the appearance. MuPDF does that in pdf-appearance.c:1040
   pdf_write_ink_appearance (+ :198 pdf_write_border_appearance, :3664
   pdf_update_appearance). Never ported.

Fixing only (1) leaves this file blank. Fixing only (2) builds an appearance
nothing draws. Both halves are required.

IMPORTANT -- "just route annotated pages to hayro" does NOT work, measured not
assumed: hayro gates every annot behind /AP -> /N at
hayro-interpret-0.7.0/src/interpret/mod.rs:157, so it paints 0/25 on this file.

Maintainer's call (this session): port from MuPDF rather than write from spec,
to save tokens and avoid debugging from scratch. MuPDF vendored sparse+shallow
at crates/kopitiam-pdf/vendor/mupdf (commit 5fe54ce, gitignored, source/pdf +
include/mupdf only, 8.1MB).

Licence note: MuPDF is AGPL-3.0 (Artifex); a translation is a derivative work.
Already the case for crates/kopitiam-pdf/src/mupdf/ -- consistent with the
existing tree and with CLAUDE.md's "cannot be relicensed off AGPL" note.

Test asset: ~/Desktop/test-annotation.pdf (51pp, 25 Ink annots on page 1,
classic xref, no ObjStm, no XRef streams). Should be copied into the repo as a
fixture so the example doubles as a regression gate.

note.content:
LICENSE SPLIT (authoritative, ai.google.dev/gemma/terms): the Gemma family is NOT uniformly GPLv3-compatible.
- Gemma 4: Apache-2.0 (OSI) → AGPLv3-compatible → OK to make default + BUNDLE/redistribute with kopitiam.
- Gemma 1/2/3/3n + others: 'Gemma Terms of Use' custom license, NOT OSI. Section 3.2 + Prohibited Use Policy: 'You must include the use restrictions ... as an enforceable provision in any agreement governing the use and/or distribution.' Passing restrictions downstream violates GPLv3/AGPLv3 §7 (no further restrictions) → INCOMPATIBLE. kopitiam must NOT bundle or default to these; they may only be USER-SUPPLIED GGUF (same opt-in path as Qwen), where kopitiam never distributes the weights.
RECOMMENDATION: default = Gemma 4 family only (gemma-4-E2B on-device; larger Gemma-4 variants for stronger CPUs). Older Gemma + Qwen = user-supplied-GGUF only. Maincoder-1B/MiniCPM5-1B/North-mini-code (all Apache-2.0) remain compatible bundleable alternatives.

note.content:
CORRECTION + SHARPENING (verified against the tree on 2026-07-25, not taken from another bead's notes):

My original framing — 'a Gemma GGUF may well load clean and emit garbage' — was OVERSTATED at the time of writing, and is becoming TRUE as the accidental backstops come down. The accurate picture:

TWO GATES were incidentally catching non-Qwen models. Neither was designed as an architecture check.
- QUANT GATE: GONE. bd-uij's comment records gguf.rs mapping only F32/F16/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/BF16, so K-quant files hard-failed at parse. That is NO LONGER TRUE in the working tree — dtype_from_ggml_type now maps ids 10-15 to Q2_K..Q8_K (the bd-3t0 K-quant work). Modern K-quant GGUFs parse today.
- TOKENIZER GATE: still standing. kopitiam-runtime/src/gguf_tokenizer.rs accepts `tokenizer.ggml.model == "gpt2"` only. Most Gemma GGUFs are SentencePiece, so they still fail here — loudly, which is the correct outcome, but by accident rather than by design.

THE TIMING POINT, AND WHY THIS BEAD IS URGENT: bd-v3x item 2 is 'add SentencePiece tokenizer support'. The moment that lands, the LAST accidental guard is gone — and a Gemma GGUF will parse, tokenize, load into QwenModel, and generate confident nonsense with nothing left to stop it. THIS GATE MUST LAND BEFORE OR TOGETHER WITH THE SPM TOKENIZER WORK, not after. Sequenced any later and there is a window where the product silently lies.

OPEN QUESTION WORTH ANSWERING WHILE BUILDING THIS (a claim I am NOT making, only flagging): llama-3.2-1b-instruct-q4_0 is in the shipped catalog and sitting in ~/.cache/kopitiam/models, and it is gpt2-BPE + Q4_0, so it presumably loads and runs through QwenModel TODAY. But Qwen2 and Llama are not the same dense architecture — Qwen2 carries QKV biases, Llama does not. Either bridge.rs handles that difference correctly, or the second catalog model has been producing subtly wrong output all along. Someone should establish which, with a reference comparison, before the whitelist is written — because the answer decides whether 'llama' belongs on it.

note.content:
PROGRESS, commit ce74f2b1be: the wgpu matmul kernel exists, is correctness-checked against its CPU twin at real transformer shapes, and - more importantly - is MEASURED. The measurements change the plan.

MEASURED on Intel integrated GPU vs 14 CPU cores, SmolLM2-360M real shapes, timings INCLUDE upload+readback:
  decode  attn q/o     (1 tok)   cpu   443us   gpu 1.88ms   0.24x   LOSS
  decode  mlp gate/up  (1 tok)   cpu  1.28ms   gpu 3.20ms   0.40x   LOSS
  decode  mlp down     (1 tok)   cpu  1.29ms   gpu 2.86ms   0.45x   LOSS
  decode  output head  (1 tok)   cpu 25.67ms   n/a - exceeds binding limit
  prefill attn q/o    (33 tok)   cpu 12.89ms   gpu 3.72ms   3.46x   WIN
  prefill mlp gate/up (33 tok)   cpu 40.83ms   gpu 7.77ms   5.26x   WIN

CONCLUSION: do NOT offload uniformly. A decode step is one row of activations and cannot amortise moving a weight matrix; a 33-token prefill does 33x the arithmetic against the same upload and wins outright. Offloading everything - the obvious reading of the original request - would make chat 2-4x SLOWER.

REMAINING WORK, in value order:
1. OUTPUT HEAD, QUANTIZED + RESIDENT. It is 49152x960 and costs 25.67ms per token on CPU - more than every other decode matmul combined, so it IS the chat lag. It cannot go to the GPU as f32 at all: 188MB against this adapter's 128MB max_storage_buffer_binding_size. Keeping it Q8_0 on the device is ~47MB, which fits. This needs a q8 matmul kernel (dequantise in-shader) plus residency. Highest value by a wide margin.
2. PREFILL OFFLOAD. Wire matmul_nt into kopitiam-runtime's linear() for the seq>1 case only, guarded on Executor::has_gpu(). Straightforward given the kernel exists; worth 3.5-5.3x on prompt ingestion.
3. RESIDENT WEIGHTS for decode. Upload each weight once at model load. Ownership/lifetime design question - a GpuLinear owning its device buffer - deliberately not smuggled in with the first kernel.
4. TILED KERNEL. The current shader is one invocation per output element with a plain dot product. Shared-memory tiling would raise the prefill win further, but it is a multiplier on (2), not a prerequisite.

BUG FIXED EN ROUTE, found by benchmarking rather than review: wgpu treats an over-limit storage binding as a validation error and PANICS, aborting the process instead of returning Err for the cascade. The output head triggers it exactly. matmul_nt_gpu now checks device limits up front and refuses with InvalidInput so the Executor falls to CPU; regression test constructs a weight one row past whatever the local adapter's limit is, so it holds on any device.

TERMUX: confirmed again - cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android passes. No gating was ever needed for compilation. Note Termux typically has no usable Vulkan driver, so the cascade lands on CPU there regardless; the lag this work addresses is the desktop case.

COMPARISON DISCIPLINE (maintainer's instruction): the hybrid path must be compared to llama.cpp, and that is now possible - bd-b9x is fixed, so our CPU forward pass agrees with llama.cpp. docs/REFERENCE-ORACLE.md documents the oracle. Any offload landing in the forward pass must be checked three ways: GPU vs our CPU twin element-wise, and end-to-end output vs llama.cpp.

note.content:
FIXED. Bigger than expected, and it partly invalidates the GPU headline from bd-jrq - saying so here rather than letting the nicer number stand.

MEASURED, CPU-only path (--no-default-features, the Termux case):
                                  before     after
  'The capital of France is'       6.77s     1.39s    4.9x
  '...over the lazy'               7.03s     1.84s    3.8x
  token_embd resident            188.7MB    50.1MB    3.8x smaller
  weights load (gpu path)          570ms     418ms
Output byte-identical across cpu-only, gpu, and llama.cpp.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PLAN. It said to load a SECOND handle via load_matmul_weight while keeping the f32 one for gather_rows, and claimed that would reduce memory. That was WRONG - it would have held both the 188MB f32 AND the 50MB quantized, i.e. worse. The caveat at the bottom of the bead turned out to be the actual fix: make gather_rows read quantized tables directly.

WHAT LANDED:
1. Tensor::gather_rows now decodes ONLY the requested rows from a block-quantized table. A row is a whole number of blocks, so row r is exactly blocks_per_row consecutive blocks at r*blocks_per_row and decodes on its own. A forward pass reads one row per token - often one total during decode - so dequantizing all 49152 rows to get them was the whole waste. Refuses a straddling row or a strided/offset view rather than returning wrong rows.
2. ModelWeights::load takes token_embd through load_matmul_weight, so it stays Q8_0 where a fused kernel exists and still falls back to f32 where none does (the 1.7B's Q6_K). Win or no-op, never a regression. The tied output_weight clone now shares quantized storage instead of duplicating an f32 expansion.

HONEST CONSEQUENCE FOR bd-jrq: the GPU output head measured 4.9x against the OLD cpu path. Against the fixed one it is 1.39s vs 1.31s - about 6%. The GPU kernel is still correct, still tested, and still the right foundation for larger models and for prefill offload (3.9-5.9x, bd-2c2), but on THIS model fixing the CPU path mattered far more than offloading it. Anyone reading bd-jrq's numbers should read this too.

Gates: 156 tensor + 146 runtime + 70 ai green, clippy -D warnings clean in both feature states, aarch64-linux-android clean in both, netfetch canonical gate green on real weights.
note.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad

note.content:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-13. Two independent hang paths, both real, both need fixing.

PATH 1 — the deadlock (primary suspect for what I hit):
  daemon/git_lane.rs fail_sync():
      sync_in_progress = false;
      consecutive_failures += 1;
      dirty = true;              // keep dirty so we retry after backoff
  daemon/runtime/server/waiters.rs flush_sync_waiters() releases a waiter ONLY when
      !dirty && !sync_in_progress
  So a sync that FAILS sets dirty=true, the waiter's release condition can never be
  true, and the retry fails again -> dirty=true again. Backoff caps at ~32s and
  retries forever. The SyncWait waiter is parked FOREVER. bn sync blocks until you
  kill it. There is no timeout anywhere: client send() has none, the daemon parks
  the responder in a HashMap with no deadline, and nothing ever tells the waiter
  'the sync keeps failing'.

PATH 2 — no timeout on the push subprocess:
  git/gix_compat.rs subprocess_push() does cmd.output() with NO deadline. If git
  stalls (TCP connect hangs, TLS handshake stalls, ssh waits), sync_in_progress
  stays TRUE forever and the same waiter never releases. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
  stops credential PROMPTS but does nothing about a stalled transfer.

Both end in the same place: bn sync never returns and never says why.

WHAT THE FIX MUST DO (not just add a timeout — the deadlock is the real bug):
  1. Wake waiters on FAILURE, not only on success, and tell them it failed:
     consecutive_failures + the last error. A command that waits must be able to
     report 'still failing' instead of hanging.
  2. Deadline on the SyncWait waiter, with --timeout on bn sync.
  3. Deadline on the git push subprocess. Consider git-native
     http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime for stalled transfers PLUS a hard process
     watchdog (covers ssh and pre-transfer hangs).
  4. On timeout, print the actual state: dirty, sync_in_progress,
     consecutive_failures, last error, remote URL. Exit non-zero.

note.content:
FIXED in commit 406cd3ed44. Root cause: WRONG RoPE PAIRING CONVENTION for llama-architecture models.

rope.rs implemented split-half (NEOX) exclusively and its docs asserted 'LLaMA and every model derived from it - including every Qwen release - uses split-half'. Only the Qwen half is true. Per llama.cpp's llama_model_rope_type (src/llama-model.cpp, switch commented 'use what we call a normal RoPE, operating on pairs of consecutive head values'), LLM_ARCH_LLAMA is NORM/interleaved and LLM_ARCH_QWEN2 is NEOX/split-half. SmolLM2 reports general.architecture=llama, so DEFAULT_MODEL_ID ran with mispositioned Q and K.

The trap underneath the trap: HuggingFace LlamaAttention really does use rotate_half (split-half) in Python, but convert_hf_to_gguf.py PERMUTES the Q/K rows so ggml's interleaved rotation reproduces it. Reading the HF modelling code and concluding split-half is right about the architecture and wrong about the file.

Why it hid: at position 0 the angle is 0 so both conventions are the identity; error grows with position. Short prompts stayed correct ('The capital of France is' -> ' Paris', '...over the lazy' -> ' dog') while long ones degraded, which reads as 'small weak model'. It is also invisible to shape/sanity checks since both conventions preserve each pair's norm. Both facts are now regression tests.

Found by layer-by-layer bisection against llama.cpp's eval-callback, which is what finally worked after every component had been individually verified correct in isolation:
                ours(before)   ours(after)   llama.cpp
  inp_embd        -6.247214     -6.247214    -6.247214
  attn_norm-0     -4.775917     -4.775917    -4.775916
  Qcur-0.rope    -32.685047    -37.304260   -37.306450   <- divergence starts here
  Kcur-0.rope    +59.619232    +59.988953   +59.997219
  attn_out-0     +11.727785    +11.524756   +11.535707
  blk.0.out         -236.6        -241.21      -242.45

Fix: RopeKind::{Interleaved,SplitHalf} selected per architecture by config::rope_kind_for_architecture, mirroring llama.cpp's table; element indexing transcribed from ggml's rotate_pairs. Unknown architectures keep the split-half default, documented as a guess.

A TEST WAS ASSERTING THE BUG: llama_and_qwen2_arch_with_identical_weights_produce_bit_identical_logits demanded the two architectures agree bit-for-bit because 'nothing in the forward pass branches on the arch string'. That premise WAS the bug, and the test passed for exactly as long as the bug existed. Rewritten to assert the opposite, with the reasoning recorded.

Verified: ai chat 'hello' -> 'i'm happy to assist you. what can i help you with today?'; 'What is the capital of France?' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.' 142 runtime tests green, netfetch canonical gate green, clippy -D warnings clean.

Knock-on: bd-2c2 (wgpu offload) is unblocked - the CPU forward pass now agrees with llama.cpp, so a GPU/CPU/llama.cpp three-way comparison is finally meaningful.

note.content: PARTLY FIXED, and the inventory in this bead was WRONG about two of them. kopitiam-semantic is now fully green on Windows (147 passed, 0 failed) - see commit 107e0cf320. Only the third (rust-analyzer indexing a 40-crate workspace) was genuinely environmental, and it now skips on TIMEOUT specifically while every other error still fails, so a real provider break cannot hide behind the guard. bd-klf (gguf_tokenizer vendor absence) also fixed and closed. The kvim ones are blocked on ConPTY not working on this box at all - see bd-hyk, which also carries a proposed (unapplied, unverifiable) fix for a real ':term' bug found while investigating. note.content: CORRECTION to this bead's own diagnosis (fix landed in c587071). I claimed kvim go-to-definition was broken for every Windows user. WRONG — probed instead of trusting it: on Windows file:///tmp/lib.rs -> None (what the tests hit) but file:///C:/tmp/lib.rs -> C:\tmp\lib.rs and file:///c%3A/tmp/lib.rs -> c:\tmp\lib.rs both convert fine, and jdt:// correctly drops. Real rust-analyzer on Windows sends drive-letter URIs, so gd/gr/hover was never broken in production. The tests were unix-only by accident, hardcoding file:///tmp/... and asserting /tmp/..., which quietly made the definition suite Linux-only. THE REAL DEFECT, now fixed: to_file_path() needs a drive letter on Windows, so a genuine file: URI from a Linux/Termux/WSL/container server was dropped SILENTLY and indistinguishably from the jdt: case that is meant to be dropped. Reachable because KOPITIAM targets Windows and Termux together and the server need not run on the client's platform. uri_to_path now drops on SCHEME never on platform, percent-decodes the URI path when the native converter refuses, and refuses a non-empty host (UNC) rather than stripping it into a confidently wrong local path. 6 new tests pin both platforms, cfg-splitting expectations where platforms genuinely differ instead of weakening them. kopitiam-semantic: 10 failures -> 3, the 3 left are bd-cfu's. clippy -D warnings clean.

STILL BLOCKING the FULL chain (both about kopitiam-models, which is a dep of apps/cli, NOT of kopitiam-ai — out of scope of the session's instruction, files left untouched):
1. kopitiam-models live at 0.0.1 but local source has a new src/hf.rs + changed catalog.rs/lib.rs. Needs 0.0.2 in crates/kopitiam-models/Cargo.toml (pinned inline, no workspace req to chase).
2. apps/cli/Cargo.toml:24 — kopitiam-models = { path = "../../crates/kopitiam-models" } has no version, so `kopitiam` itself cannot publish. Move to root [workspace.dependencies] with path+version, use { workspace = true } here.

NEW FINDING — publish.sh may be largely obsolete. Cargo 1.97 supports multi-package publish (cargo publish -p a -p b ...): it computes the topological order ITSELF and verifies each package against a temp registry built from its packaged siblings, so a whole chain of never-published interdependent crates can be dry-run in one shot (proved above). That removes the need for the script's hand-rolled CRATES ordering AND wait_for_index(). What stays worth keeping: the preflight checks (stale-seed, vendor/, path-dep-without-version) and publish_with_retry()'s 429 Retry-After handling, none of which cargo does. Worth an AID + a rewrite pass.

NOT DONE, still worth doing before any real publish: no crate dir carries a LICENSE file (cargo only packages files under the crate dir, so root LICENSE never travels — every tarball so far ships GPL-3.0-only with no licence text); no README on the runtime chain, so crates.io pages render blank.

Nothing committed, nothing published.

note.content:
KERNEL DONE and measured, commit 685cb2943f. The GPU half of this bead is complete; what remains is wiring it into kopitiam-runtime.

MEASURED, SmolLM2-360M output head (49152 x 960), Intel integrated GPU vs 14 CPU cores:
  one-time upload : 97.12ms
  cpu  per token  : 26.12ms
  gpu  per token  :  8.55ms   (3.06x)
  upload amortises after ~6 tokens
About 17.6ms saved per token on the dominant decode cost, paid back inside a six-token reply. For contrast the naive per-call f32 path in the same bench is a 0.24-0.45x LOSS - the entire difference is residency, not the kernel.

WHAT LANDED: ResidentBlockQ8Weight in kopitiam-gpu. Upload once at model load, dispatch per token. Deliberately expressed as GENERIC block-scaled int8 (32 quants per f32 scale) rather than named Q8_0, because kopitiam-gpu describes itself as domain-agnostic parallel-compute infrastructure and must not learn GGUF; the caller separates scales from quants. Format knowledge stays in kopitiam-runtime where the layout is already verified byte-for-byte against ggml-quants.c.

THE RISK THE TESTS ARE BUILT AROUND: WGSL has no i8, so quants travel packed four-per-u32 and the shader sign-extends by hand. Get it wrong and 0xFF reads as +255 instead of -1, every negative weight flips sign, and the model emits fluent nonsense rather than failing. Fixtures span the full signed range including -128 and -1; a fixture of small positives would pass either way.

REMAINING, to actually reach the chat:
1. Repack the GGUF Q8_0 output.weight into (scales, quants) at model load. kopitiam-tensor's dequant_q8_0 already documents the block layout; this needs the inverse split, not a dequantise.
2. Hold the ResidentBlockQ8Weight next to the model and route linear() to it for output.weight only, guarded on Executor::has_gpu(), CPU twin otherwise.
3. COMPARE AGAINST LLAMA.CPP END TO END, per the maintainer's standing instruction - not merely against our own CPU twin. docs/REFERENCE-ORACLE.md has the procedure. bd-b9x is fixed so the CPU path is a trustworthy baseline now.
4. Only then consider prefill offload (matmul_nt, worth 3.9-5.9x on prompt ingestion) and a tiled kernel.

CAVEAT worth stating plainly: 97ms of upload at model load is fine for a chat session but is pure cost for a one-shot CLI invocation that emits a couple of tokens. Whatever wires this in should decide residency lazily - on first use, or when the reply is expected to exceed ~6 tokens - rather than unconditionally at load.

note.content:
DONE and wired into the chat, commits 70e172cf9d + 00536c9ec5.

MEASURED A/B on the same binary, same prompts, greedy (gpu feature on vs --no-default-features):
                              gpu on    gpu off   speedup
  model load                   570ms      295ms   +275ms once
  'The capital of France is'   1.37s      6.77s     4.9x
  '...over the lazy'           1.68s      7.03s     4.2x
  chat, 24 tokens              5.93s     14.40s     2.4x

COMPARED TO LLAMA.CPP as instructed - not merely against our own CPU twin. Byte-identical:
  ours (hybrid) -> 'hello, how can I assist you today?'
  llama.cpp     -> 'hello, how can I assist you today?'
And every greedy completion matches between gpu-on, gpu-off and llama.cpp.

SCOPE: only the output projection is offloaded. The small decode matmuls measure 0.24-0.45x on the GPU, so offloading uniformly would have made chat 2-4x SLOWER. That is why this bead was worth splitting out of bd-2c2.

A CPU-SIDE FINDING WORTH ITS OWN BEAD fell out of this. Neither SmolLM2 ships a separate output.weight; both tie it to token_embd.weight. ModelWeights loads token_embd via load_tensor_f32 (the embedding lookup needs real floats) and the tied fallback CLONES it - so the single biggest matmul in the model has been running against a fully dequantized f32 weight, skipping the fused quantized kernel every other projection gets, and holding 188MB of f32 where 47MB of Q8_0 would do. Fixing the CPU path to keep the quantized tensor for the output projection would speed up and shrink the no-GPU case too, which matters for Termux where there is no usable Vulkan driver.

FEATURE GATE: 'gpu', default ON. Not for Termux's sake - cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android passes both with and without it, and the cascade handles a missing GPU at runtime. It exists so a lean build can say --no-default-features and skip the wgpu tree entirely.

HONESTY FIX: the CLI notice said 'Using local model on CPU' unconditionally, which stopped being true. Now reports 'hybrid CPU + GPU (output projection on GPU)' or 'CPU', from QwenModel::gpu_output_head_active().

Falls through to CPU on any GPU failure mid-session - a slower answer beats a wrong one.

Gates: 146 runtime + 11 gpu + 310 cli + 70 ai green, clippy -D warnings clean in BOTH feature states, aarch64-linux-android clean in both.
note.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad

note.content: CROSS-REFERENCE from bd-8f8: the 4.9x figure in this bead was measured against a CPU path that was itself defective - it dequantized the tied embedding/output weight to f32 and skipped the fused quantized kernel. With that fixed (bd-8f8), the GPU output head is worth about 6 percent on SmolLM2-360M, not 4.9x. The kernel remains correct and is still the right foundation for larger models and prefill offload, but the honest current value on this model is small. Do not quote the 4.9x without this correction.

note.content:
FIXED. Ported MuPDF's guard from pdf_load_obj_stm (pdf-xref.c:2213) as PdfDocument::claimed_by_objstm(): an object parsed out of object stream S is only cached when the xref still says XrefEntry::Compressed{stm_num: S}. Objects the newest xref section has superseded (now 'n' at a fresh offset) are skipped before parsing, so they can never reach the first-write-wins cache.

Regression test mupdf::xref::tests::incremental_update_supersedes_object_stream_copy + fixture incremental_update_pdf(): original body packs objs 1/2/3 into objstm 4 (xref stream 5); appended update supersedes obj 3 uncompressed with MediaBox 400 + /Annots of 5, indexed by xref stream 6 via /Prev + /Index [3 1 6 1]. Verified the test FAILS without the guard (MediaBox 200 not 400 -- same shape as the reported 3-vs-8 /Annots) and passes with it.

Gates: cargo test --release -p kopitiam-pdf = 329+1+2 pass; all 8 reverse-dep crates pass; cargo clippy --release --all-targets clean for xref.rs (4 warnings all pre-existing in doc_stream/font/page_image/stream.rs). Journal: docs/engineering-journal/2026-08-25-dropped-guards-in-a-port.md

note.content:
LOADER REALITY (from research + code read, applies to any download target):
1. QUANT GATE: kopitiam-loader/src/gguf.rs:241-252 dtype_from_ggml_type only maps F32,F16,Q4_0,Q4_1,Q5_0,Q5_1,Q8_0,BF16. K-quants (Q4_K_M/Q6_K) HARD-FAIL at parse. Most modern small GGUFs are K-quants. Bridge confirms: kopitiam-runtime/src/bridge.rs:43 handles only Q4_0|Q4_1|Q5_0|Q5_1|Q8_0.
2. TOKENIZER GATE: kopitiam-runtime/src/gguf_tokenizer.rs expects tokenizer.ggml.model=='gpt2' (byte-level BPE + merges). SentencePiece/llama tokenizers error.
=> Effectively only Qwen-style classic-quant GGUFs actually load+chat today.

gemma-4-E2B-it (https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it): Apache-2.0 CONFIRMED, but ships model.safetensors ONLY (NO GGUF), ~5B params (multi-GB). Not llama-shaped, SentencePiece tokenizer => cannot load on current runtime. Downloading it = large pull -> Echo. Do NOT wire the downloader to it yet.

Runnable-today stand-in that stays non-Qwen: MiniCPM5-1B-Q8_0.gguf (openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B-GGUF, Apache-2.0) is a supported quant (Q8_0) — BUT verify its tokenizer.ggml.model=='gpt2' first (MiniCPM base is SPM; if so it fails the tokenizer gate too). Q4_K_M variant is unsupported (K-quant).

note.content:
ONE ADDITION from a 2026-07-25 code read (bd-250.4 was filed covering this ground and is closed as a duplicate of this bead; everything else in it — placeholder sha256 gate, need for real HF coordinates, the Gemma licence split — is already captured here or in bd-250's comments):

`KOPITIAM_MODEL=gemma-...` DOES NOT ERROR — IT SILENTLY GIVES YOU QWEN. apps/cli/src/adapter.rs's select_adapter does:

    let spec = Catalog::find(&model_id).unwrap_or_else(|| Catalog::find(DEFAULT_MODEL_ID).expect(...));

So an unknown/unimplemented catalog id falls back to the default spec with NO message. `Architecture::Gemma` exists as a bare enum variant (catalog.rs:34-35) with no ModelSpec behind it, so a user who sets KOPITIAM_MODEL to any Gemma id today gets Qwen2.5-0.5B and is told nothing — SelectedAdapter::notice() reports 'Using local model on CPU: <qwen path>', which is truthful but does not mention that the model they ASKED for was silently discarded.

Small standalone fix, independent of everything else in this bead: an unknown model id should be a clear error (or at minimum a loud note naming both the requested id and the substituted one). The fallback itself is defensible — it keeps the offline path working — but it must be visible. Worth doing NOW, before any auto-download work, because it is the difference between 'Gemma isn't supported yet' and 'Gemma appeared to work'.

note.content: MODEL-SELECTION POLICY (maintainer, 2026-07-25): once Gemma runs, DEFAULT = Gemma (gemma-4-E2B-it), FALLBACK = Qwen-0.5B on devices with < 10 GB total RAM. Implement a RAM-aware tier in select_adapter: read total system RAM; >=10GB -> Gemma, <10GB -> Qwen. 10GB threshold is right because dequant-to-f32 expands gemma-4-E2B (~5B params) to ~f32 in memory (~10GB). SEQUENCING / do-not-regress: keep Qwen the working default NOW; only flip to Gemma-default when this bead's arch+SPM-tokenizer+weights land (else >=10GB machines fall back to Echo and lose today's working Qwen chat). Ship the RAM selector together with Gemma support, not before. Qwen stays as the explicit low-RAM fallback (this supersedes the earlier 'Qwen only if user supplies GGUF' — Qwen is now the bundled low-RAM fallback tier).

note.content:
POLICY REFINED (maintainer): Qwen and other Chinese-origin models (MiniCPM/openbmb, etc.) are LAST RESORT, not the fallback tier. Corrected ladder:
- Default (>=10GB RAM): Gemma (gemma-4-E2B-it) — Google, Apache-2.0.
- Low-RAM (<10GB): a LOWER-PARAMETER, license-clean (GPL-3.0-compatible: Apache-2.0/MIT), NON-Chinese model. Candidates to evaluate: smaller Gemma variants, SmolLM (HF, Apache-2.0), Phi (Microsoft, MIT) — final pick TBD, must also be loader-compatible.
- LAST RESORT only: Qwen (Alibaba) + other Chinese models.
CAVEAT: today the ONLY runnable model is Qwen (gpt2-BPE tokenizer + qwen2 arch + classic quant). The preferred non-Chinese small models mostly use SentencePiece tokenizers, so they depend on the SAME SPM-tokenizer + arch work as Gemma (this bead). So Qwen remains the INTERIM runnable stopgap until SPM+arch lands, then it demotes to last-resort. Selection stays RAM-gated (>=10GB Gemma / <10GB small non-Chinese).

note.content:
ADDITIONS from a 2026-07-25 code read (bd-250.2 was filed covering this same ground and has been closed as a duplicate of this bead — these are the only parts not already here):

1. DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY KERNELS: does kopitiam-runtime grow a SECOND concrete model type, or a trait both Qwen and Gemma implement? Today QwenConfig/QwenModel are named concretely throughout (config.rs literally sets FORMAT = "qwen-config" and its docs say it 'encodes one specific architecture family'), and kopitiam-ai's LocalAdapter is written against them. A copy-pasted second transformer is the tempting and wrong answer. Per CLAUDE.md, propose the architecture and record an AID BEFORE writing the forward pass — this is the real design work, the kernels are the easy half.

2. VALIDATION METHOD. 'It emits plausible English' proves nothing — a subtly wrong forward pass does exactly that (wrong RMSNorm convention, missing sqrt(hidden_size) embedding scale, SwiGLU where GeGLU belongs). The honest check is greedy decoding with a fixed prompt and fixed seed compared against llama.cpp's output for the SAME GGUF file, token for token. Worth building that comparison harness as part of this bead, not after.

3. SCOPE FENCE: gemma-4-E2B is multimodal (text+image+audio). Text-only path first, explicitly out of scope here — worth stating so it does not creep.

note.content:
REFUTED, and the bead's own hypothesis was wrong. Not a pre-tokenizer bug. Not a runtime bug at all.

WHAT I CHECKED, all against the vendored reference rather than by reasoning (llama.cpp now vendored at crates/kopitiam-ai/vendor/llama.cpp):

  tokenizer.ggml.pre='smollm' -> llama.cpp LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_SMOLLM adds a leading '\p{N}' pass and ends '\s+(?!\S)' where ours ends '\s+'. REAL difference, but harmless here: our encoder ALREADY splits digits individually ('12345' -> 1,2,3,4,5), and the ChatML pieces tokenize correctly ('system\n' -> ['system','\n'], 'assistant\n' -> ['ass','istant','\n'] — 'assistant' has no single-token id in this vocab, so that split is right).
  RoPE: split-half/NEOX convention correct; tables verified numerically against hand computation at positions 0,1,5,12,19,33,100 with the real params (rope_dim 64, theta 100000) — max abs diff 0e0.
  Config: every value matches the file. 360M theta 100000, 1.7B theta 130000, both read correctly. head_dim/heads/kv_heads/ffn/layers/eps all correct.
  Tensor primitives: transpose+matmul vs hand loops at real shapes (15x19x19x64), softmax normalisation, scalar-rank-0 division, rms_norm, and the causal mask BROADCASTING over all 15 heads (the one my first probe could not have caught, since the mask is all-zeros for seq=1 and for the final row).
  KV cache: concat on dim 1, verified. Prefill vs one-token-at-a-time agree exactly.
  Quantization vs ggml-quants.c: dequant_q4_k matches dequantize_row_q4_K byte for byte, get_scale_min_k4 matches including the q[j-0] subtlety, dequant_q6_k matches including the SIGNED 'as i8' scales trap.

WHERE I WENT WRONG. I built a length ladder with 'The weather is mild.' repeated five times and read the degradation as a runtime bug. That prompt is precisely the pattern that makes induction heads copy, so it measured repetition, not length. I rebuilt it with distinct sentences and still called it conclusive — also wrong, because unrelated prefix legitimately shifts a 360M's distribution ('Paris' at rank 63 of 49152 is still top-0.1 percent). Canonical completions settle it: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy' -> ' dog.' and an 18-token 'Once upon a time...near the' -> ' sea. She had a'. The runtime is fine at these lengths.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED, and is NOT a runtime defect: SmolLM2-1.7B-Q4_K_M, given a correct ChatML prompt, puts <|im_end|>=18.50 and <|im_start|>=17.75 as its top two logits right after '<|im_start|>assistant\n' — it wants to end the turn rather than answer. The SAME file does raw completion correctly (' Paris, the city of light, the'; ' dog') so its weights are being applied correctly. The 360M in the same code path is sane there ('The'=13.70, 'Yes', 'A'). So this is specific to that model/quantisation's chat behaviour, not to our stack. Filed as a separate observation, not a runtime bug.

LANDED FROM THIS: the netfetch harness now asserts a canonical completion, not merely 'the chain ran'. That hole is what let a plausible-looking PASS coexist with gibberish and sent this whole hunt off. Also, vendoring llama.cpp restored ggml-vocab-qwen2.gguf, so bd-klf's three tests pass locally now (they will still fail on a fresh clone, since vendor/ is gitignored — that bead stands).
